## Overview

In this notebook, we address three questions:

1.  How does tumor purity relate to `PDCD1` expression, T cell–inflamed GEP scores, and TMB measured from bulk tumor samples?
2.  Could differences in tumor purity partly explain the biomarker associations with treatment response (`BOR`: Responder `R` vs. Non-Responder `NR`) observed in RQ2 and RQ3?
3.  Does adjusting gene expression for tumor purity improve the biological interpretation of these biomarkers?

## Setup and data inspection

```{r}
#| label: setup

library(immunedeconv)
library(limma)
library(DESeq2)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)

# Load prepared IMvigor210 dataset
prep <- readRDS("../data/processed/imvigor210_prepared.rds")

tpm <- as.matrix(prep$tpm)
clinical <- as.data.frame(prep$clinical)

cat("TPM matrix dimensions:\n")
print(dim(tpm))

cat("\nTPM value range (should be linear for ESTIMATE):\n")
print(range(tpm, na.rm = TRUE))

cat("\nClinical data dimensions:\n")
print(dim(clinical))

cat("\nClinical variables:\n")
print(colnames(clinical))
```

```{r}
#| label: align-samples

# Verify that all clinical sample IDs are present in the expression matrix
stopifnot(all(clinical$sample_id %in% colnames(tpm)))

# Reorder expression columns to match the clinical table
tpm <- tpm[, match(clinical$sample_id, colnames(tpm)), drop = FALSE]

# Explicitly verify sample alignment
stopifnot(identical(clinical$sample_id, colnames(tpm)))

cat("Samples aligned:", ncol(tpm), "\n")
cat("Missing TPM values:", sum(is.na(tpm)), "\n")

cat("\nBOR distribution:\n")
print(table(clinical$BOR, useNA = "ifany"))

cat("\nTMB summary:\n")
print(summary(clinical$TMB))
```

```{r}
#| label: transform-expression

# Log2-transform TPM for downstream linear modeling and GEP calculation.

expr <- log2(tpm + 1)
```

```{r}
#| label: extract-biomarkers

# Import GEP scores from RQ2
GEP_scores <- readRDS('../data/processed/RQ2_GEP_scores_with_meta.rds')

# Tumor mutational burden
TMB <- clinical$TMB

# Confirm PDCD1 is present and extract expression
stopifnot("PDCD1" %in% rownames(expr))
PD1 <- as.numeric(expr["PDCD1", ])



# Combine into a single analysis dataframe
df <- data.frame(
  sample = clinical$sample_id,
  TMB = TMB,
  PD1 = PD1,
  GEP_scores = GEP_scores,
  Response = factor(clinical$BOR, levels = c("NR", "R"))
)

stopifnot(identical(df$sample, colnames(expr)))
summary(df)
```

### Helper functions

```{r}
#| label: helper-functions

plot_Response_boxplot <- function(data, variable, y_label, test_result, title = NULL) {
  ggplot(data, aes(x = Response, y = .data[[variable]], fill = Response)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.12, alpha = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = Inf, y = Inf,
      label = paste0("Wilcoxon p = ", signif(test_result$p.value, 3)),
      hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5
    ) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      x = "Best Overall Response (BOR)",
      y = y_label
    ) +
    theme_minimal()
}

plot_association <- function(data, x, y, x_label, y_label, cor_test, title = NULL) {
  rho <- unname(cor_test$estimate)

  ggplot(data, aes(x = .data[[x]], y = .data[[y]])) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#2C3E50") +
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = Inf, y = Inf,
      label = paste0(
        "Spearman rho = ", round(rho, 2),
        "\np = ", signif(cor_test$p.value, 3)
      ),
      hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.3
    ) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      x = x_label,
      y = y_label
    ) +
    theme_minimal()
}
```

## 2. Estimate tumor purity

We estimate tumor purity from the linear TPM matrix using ESTIMATE (`immunedeconv::deconvolute_estimate()`), which infers immune and stromal infiltration from bulk gene expression.

```{r}
#| label: estimate-purity

purity <- deconvolute_estimate(tpm)

cat("ESTIMATE output rows:\n")
print(rownames(purity))

# Identify and extract the tumor purity row
purity_row <- grep("purity", rownames(purity), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)
if (length(purity_row) != 1) {
  stop("Could not identify exactly one tumor-purity row in the ESTIMATE output.")
}

tumor_purity <- as.numeric(purity[purity_row, ])
names(tumor_purity) <- colnames(purity)

# Align tumor purity estimates with the analysis dataframe
tumor_purity <- tumor_purity[colnames(tpm)]
stopifnot(identical(names(tumor_purity), df$sample))

df$purity <- tumor_purity
summary(df$purity)
```

### Does tumor purity itself differ between response groups?

```{r}
#| label: purity-vs-response

purity_Response_test <- wilcox.test(purity ~ Response, data = df)
purity_Response_test

plot_Response_boxplot(
  df, "purity",
  y_label = "Estimated tumor purity (ESTIMATE)",
  test_result = purity_Response_test,
  title = "Tumor purity by treatment response"
)
```

## 3. How strongly are the biomarkers related to tumor purity?

We quantify the monotonic relationship between estimated tumor purity and each candidate biomarker using Spearman rank correlation.

```{r}
#| label: purity-correlations

TMB_purity_cor <- cor.test(
  df$purity, df$TMB,
  method = "spearman",
  exact = FALSE,
  use = "complete.obs"
)

PD1_purity_cor <- cor.test(
  df$purity, df$PD1,
  method = "spearman",
  exact = FALSE,
  use = "complete.obs"
)

GEP_purity_cor <- cor.test(
  df$purity, df$GEP_scores,
  method = "spearman",
  exact = FALSE,
  use = "complete.obs"
)

TMB_purity_cor
PD1_purity_cor
GEP_purity_cor
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-purity-correlations

plot_association(
  df, "purity", "TMB",
  x_label = "Estimated tumor purity",
  y_label = "Tumor mutational burden (mut/Mb)",
  cor_test = TMB_purity_cor,
  title = "Tumor purity vs. TMB"
)

plot_association(
  df, "purity", "PD1",
  x_label = "Estimated tumor purity",
  y_label = "PDCD1 expression (log2 TPM + 1)",
  cor_test = PD1_purity_cor,
  title = "Tumor purity vs. PDCD1 expression"
)

plot_association(
  df, "purity", "GEP_scores",
  x_label = "Estimated tumor purity",
  y_label = "T cell-inflamed GEP score",
  cor_test = GEP_purity_cor,
  title = "Tumor purity vs. T cell-inflamed GEP score"
)
```

## 4. Sensitivity analysis: adjusting expression for tumor purity

As a sensitivity analysis, we regress out the linear component associated with estimated tumor purity from the gene-expression matrix using `limma::removeBatchEffect()`. We then re-extract `PDCD1` and recompute the 18-gene GEP score from the adjusted expression matrix to assess how much of the response association is driven by cellular composition.

```{r}
#| label: purity-adjust-expression

# Remove the linear effect of tumor purity from the expression matrix
expr_adjusted <- removeBatchEffect(
  expr,
  covariates = matrix(df$purity, ncol = 1)
)

# Re-extract PDCD1 and recalculate GEP score on purity-adjusted expression
PD1_adjusted <- as.numeric(expr_adjusted["PDCD1", ])

GEP_expr_adjusted <- expr_adjusted[GEP_genes_present, , drop = FALSE]
GEP_expr_adjusted_scaled <- t(scale(t(GEP_expr_adjusted)))
GEP_scores_adjusted <- colMeans(GEP_expr_adjusted_scaled, na.rm = TRUE)

df_adjusted <- data.frame(
  sample = clinical$sample_id,
  PD1 = PD1_adjusted,
  GEP_scores = GEP_scores_adjusted,
  Response = df$Response
)

stopifnot(identical(df_adjusted$sample, colnames(expr_adjusted)))
```

### Re-evaluate association with treatment response (`BOR`)

```{r}
#| label: adjusted-response-tests

PD1_Response_adjusted_test <- wilcox.test(PD1 ~ Response, data = df_adjusted)
GEP_Response_adjusted_test <- wilcox.test(GEP_scores ~ Response, data = df_adjusted)

PD1_Response_adjusted_test
GEP_Response_adjusted_test

plot_Response_boxplot(
  df_adjusted, "PD1",
  y_label = "Purity-adjusted PDCD1 expression",
  test_result = PD1_Response_adjusted_test,
  title = "Purity-adjusted PDCD1 expression by response"
)

plot_Response_boxplot(
  df_adjusted, "GEP_scores",
  y_label = "Purity-adjusted T cell-inflamed GEP score",
  test_result = GEP_Response_adjusted_test,
  title = "Purity-adjusted GEP score by response"
)
```

## 5. Summary comparison: Unadjusted vs. Purity-Adjusted

```{r}
#| label: summary-table

fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "—", formatC(p, format = "e", digits = 2))

summary_tbl <- data.frame(
  Biomarker = c("TMB", "PDCD1 (PD-1)", "T cell–inflamed GEP", "Tumor purity (ESTIMATE)"),
  Rho       = c("0.12", "-0.69", "-0.77", "—"),
  P_cor     = fmt_p(c(TMB_purity_cor$p.value, PD1_purity_cor$p.value, GEP_purity_cor$p.value, NA)),
  P_unadj   = fmt_p(c(TMB_Response_test$p.value, PD1_Response_test$p.value, GEP_Response_test$p.value, purity_Response_test$p.value)),
  P_adj     = fmt_p(c(NA, PD1_Response_adjusted_test$p.value, GEP_Response_adjusted_test$p.value, NA))
)

knitr::kable(
  summary_tbl,
  format = "pipe",
  col.names = c("Biomarker", "Spearman ρ", "Purity cor. p", "Unadjusted BOR p", "Purity-adjusted BOR p"),
  align = "lcccc"
)
```

## 6. Discussion and interpretation

-   **How tumor purity influences bulk RNA-seq biomarkers:** Bulk RNA-seq measures an average expression profile across malignant, immune, and stromal cells. Because `PDCD1` and the 18-gene GEP primarily reflect infiltrating T cells and IFN-$\gamma$–driven immune activity, higher tumor purity dilutes immune transcripts, typically producing a strong negative correlation between estimated purity and immune biomarker levels. In contrast, TMB is derived from somatic mutations in tumor DNA rather than immune-cell RNA, so its relationship with purity behaves differently.
-   **Impact on RQ2 and RQ3 associations:** I have to check their results, but if they also found an association: both remain significantly associated with treatment response after regressing out purity ($p = 1.60 \times 10^{-3}$ and $p = 2.78 \times 10^{-5}$), while purity itself does not differ between responders and non-responders ($p = 0.179$). This shows that the associations found in RQ2 and RQ3 are not just an artifact of bulk immune-cell dilution, but reflect actual differences in T-cell activation.
-   **Should we adjust for tumor purity?** Not automatically. Unlike a technical batch effect, cellular composition in the tumor microenvironment is a core biological determinant of anti-PD-L1 efficacy. Regressing out tumor purity removes genuine biological signal (the presence of infiltrating T cells) and changes the scientific question from *"Does total immune infiltration/activation associate with response?"* to *"Does residual immune gene expression beyond bulk cellular composition associate with response?"*.
